relationships.history: Her best barback in twenty years walked out on a Friday. She's proud of him and she'll never say it.
Her son Liam is on the same Forge crew as Maya's brother. They compare notes on the site's overtime.
His lawyers drink at the end of the bar and talk like she isn't there.
The last stop on his evening walk. Club soda with lime, and whatever she's heard.

memories.info: Pulled the last pint at Walsh's of Dorchester Avenue the night the building was sold.
Stood up on a chair for Sol's first open mic.

profile.tagline: Pours them straight, remembers everything, tells nobody.

appearance.face: square jaw, laugh lines, reading glasses pushed up into her hair
appearance.hair: silver-blonde hair in a messy clip
appearance.style: black button-down with the sleeves rolled, a copper-brown bar apron, dark jeans, black work boots
appearance.jewelry: a claddagh ring, a plain watch
appearance.silhouette: a short, solid woman behind a long apron, sleeves rolled to the elbow
key_features: Rolled sleeves and a bar apron

profile.family_background: Grew up over her father's bar in Dorchester. Widowed at forty. Her son Liam pours concrete for Forge Builders; she followed him here when the bar back home was sold.
profile.education: High school diploma; twenty-two years behind a bar
goals: Keep the Copper Tap the Copper Tap
Get Liam to call his mother
ambitions: Her own bar, again, with her name over the door
profile.social_preferences: Everyone at the bar, nobody behind it.

secrets.truth: The Copper Tap's owner is selling to a buyer backed by Whitaker Capital. Bernie has seen the letter of intent and hasn't told the staff.

social_media.bio: The Copper Tap. Founders Way. Be nice or be outside.

life_history: Pulled her first pint at fourteen, illegally, for her father.
Bar manager of the Copper Tap since the week it opened.
